**Asia pre-market reactions — Thursday, 12 November 2026**

**TL;DR**

- **All four markets closed lower, and the damage is concentrated in one place: semiconductors.** Taiwan -2.63% (43,091.87), Hong Kong -1.26% (24,008.55), Japan -0.70% (60,819.36), Korea -0.61% (5,342.73).
- The driver was Nvidia, which fell **-6.88% in the US pre-market on 7.58m shares** after the Jensen Huang controversy broke overnight, and every large move in the tables below sits in that complex - or in gold, where spot broke below US$4,000/oz on a Fed 50bp-hike repricing.
- **Taiwan was the most consequential market** and the only real sector break:
- electronic components -5.97%, six PCB and board names locked at the TWSE -10% limit, TSMC -2.30% (roughly 440 points of the index) and ASE -5.02%.
- It is the second session of violent chop after a -12.19% week, with the NT$500bn National Financial Stabilization Fund already deployed.
- **The caveat that changes how to read it:** the index damage is much smaller than the table implies, because the two biggest *corporate* events of the session were earnings in opposite directions - Resonac +12.48% on a sharply raised FY26 forecast (core operating profit guidance lifted to ~¥250bn) against Rakuten Bank -14.87% and Dexerials -16.57% on guidance left unchanged - and none of the three has a US-listed proxy.
- Also treat the top numbers as artefacts where they are limit prints:
- Korea's +29.93% is the KRX daily limit on a thin-float preferred line, and Taiwan's -10.00% is the TWSE limit.

- **US read-across.** The overnight move is already partly priced in the US pre-market, but only the semiconductor leg of it:
- Nvidia -6.88% on 7.58m shares, SK hynix -3.97% on 309,519, Alibaba -4.26% on 341,317, TSM -2.26% on 62,292 and the South Korea ETF -1.94% on 186,046.
- The gold leg is not priced (GLD -0.95% on 109,056 versus -10.35% in Hong Kong gold equities), and neither is the earnings dispersion.

- **Exposed US names.** TSM -2.26% pre-market (62,292 shares) carries the Taiwan PCB/AI-hardware rout; SKHY -3.97% (309,519) carries the Korean semiconductor complex; BABA -4.26% (341,317) carries the Hong Kong/China risk-off.
- For the day's biggest single mover, HKEX:2259 Zijin Gold International, the only US-listed line is the OTC ADR ZJGIY - **no material US pre-market print yet**.
- **Exposed US sectors.** Electronic Technology / Semiconductor is where the Asian damage concentrates (Nvidia, TSM, SK hynix, and the OTC ADRs for Ibiden and Square Enix, neither of which has a pre-market print).
- The largest US pre-market moves overall - ADXN +60.1%, YMT -15.4%, BZ -17.8% - are idiosyncratic name events, not this read-across.
- **The overnight implication.** The US pre-market has priced the Nvidia leg of the Asia move, and has not priced the Japan earnings dispersion or the gold-equity break - neither has a US proxy.
- The residual risk sits in the US session, not in the Asia open; a Taiwan stabilization-fund headline is the one overnight catalyst that could re-open the Asia gap.

**What matters today**

**Top 3 real events (sourced catalyst)**

- KRX:18064K +29.93% - HANJIN KAL preferred - Hoban Group vs Walter Cho stake battle;
- the line locked at the KRX +30% daily limit again, is a thin-float non-voting preferred, was designated an investment-warning issue on 5 Nov and had trading suspended on 10 Nov.
- TSE:4980 -16.57% - Dexerials - FY26 H1 results released 12 Nov: H1 profit fell on weaker display and ARF volumes and higher growth-investment costs;
- FY26 guidance unchanged at ¥123.0bn sales and ¥40.0bn business profit.
- TSE:5838 -14.87% - Rakuten Bank - H1 results announced 11 Nov: net profit ¥43.2bn (+27.0% YoY), but post-reorganisation EPS guidance left unchanged and the credit-card outlook soft;
- the revised forecast fell short of expectations. Morgan Stanley published a tactical note on 12 Nov (Equal-weight, PT ¥6,860).

**Top 3 artifact traps (do not quote)**

- `SAPSE:4502` Takeda **+23.26%** - a frozen regional-venue print, byte-identical to the 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11 artifacts; the number to quote is the Tokyo line, `TSE:4502` **+2.28%**.
- The same rule applies to the two biggest numbers in today's raw Japanese scan: `NAG:6999` Koa **+64.70%** (Tokyo line -2.91%) and `NAG:3974` SCAT **+65.93%** (Tokyo line -2.00%).
- `KRX:18064K` Hanjin KAL preferred **+29.93%** - the KRX +30% daily limit on a thin-float preferred line, not a re-rating:
- the common line closed ¥31,650, up ¥150 (+0.48%) the same day, and KRX has already flagged the preferred as an investment-warning issue.
- The **index levels themselves** have a live source conflict: the MCP bridge prints `^TWII` **+0.89%** and `^HSI` **-2.23%** because its `previous_close` is one session stale.
- The published numbers are the TAIEX **-2.63%** (43,091.87, per CNA/Focus Taiwan and three further Taiwanese sources) and the Hang Seng **-1.26%** (24,008.55, per Xinhua, FT and Zhitong Finance).

**Flags**

- **The Japanese regional prints are still the biggest misquote risk, and they are not shrinking.** All 49 regional-venue rows in today's scan (33 Nagoya, 11 Fukuoka, 5 Sapporo) diverged from their Tokyo line.
- Eight were resolved against their TSE line and dropped in favour of the primary listing; 28 had no TSE line at all and were dropped entirely.
- Takeda printed +23.26% on Sapporo against +2.28% on Tokyo, Koa +64.70% on Nagoya against -2.91%, and SCAT +65.93% on Nagoya against -2.00%.
- The Takeda print is byte-identical to the last two artifacts - it is a frozen quote, not a live one.
- **Taiwan's -10% cluster is a price limit, not a market.** Three published names sit at exactly -10.00% and six more within 0.2pp of it;
- two of the published names are Taipei Exchange listings rather than TWSE primary names. The electronic-components sector fell 5.97%,
- and CNA names Nanya PCB, Hermes-Epitek, Taiwan Union Technology and Unimicron specifically - so the cluster is one AI-hardware story told ten times, not ten independent re-ratings.
- **Korea's two biggest published moves are preferred lines, and they are separate securities from their common lines.** Hanjin KAL preferred (+29.93%) and Korean Air preferred (+19.16%) have no voting rights and a thin float;
- the Korean Air common line was a separate, ordinary move. Kleannara preferred fell 21% the same session.
- A multi-day series on these lines is a limit artefact, not a series of fundamental re-ratings.
- **The index levels have a live source conflict.** The MCP bridge prints `^TWII` +0.89% and `^HSI` -2.23% because its `previous_close` is one session stale;
- the published chart-derived numbers are -2.63% and -1.26%, and both are confirmed by same-day press (CNA/Focus Taiwan for the TAIEX; Xinhua, FT and Zhitong Finance for the Hang Seng).
- Only the chart numbers are published.
- **The US OTC ADR fields are not a substitute for the primary line.** The `KGBLY` field carries a -32.47% session change for HKEX:1888 Kingboard Laminates, whose own ADR last traded on 2026-11-10 unchanged at $125;
- the published Hong Kong line is -5.56%.
- Similarly, the exact-company OTC ADRs for Ibiden (IBIDY), Square Enix (SQNNY), Zijin Gold (ZJGIY) and Japan Tobacco (JAPAY) all show a 11 November session change against a 12 November Asian session - they are a day behind.
- **The macro tape behind all four markets.** Nvidia -6.88% in the US pre-market on 7.58m shares after the Jensen Huang controversy;
- US October CPI +0.3% m/m, above expectations, pushing CME FedWatch to a 100% chance of a December hike and a 12.7% chance of 50bp, with Governor Waller flagging a 50bp move;
- the 10-year Treasury yield back to 4.998% (toward 5%) and the dollar index at 102.89; spot gold below US$4,000/oz, which is what broke the Hong Kong gold complex.
- **Hong Kong's table is not a representative sample of the market.** Only 20 names in the whole market cleared the screen (5 up, 15 down) against a HK$15.7bn market-cap floor, and the largest gainer (HKEX:9900 Hong Kong Zcloud +7.96%) is a HK$2.1bn construction name with no identified catalyst.
- **Japan's index and Japan's book disagreed today.** The Nikkei fell 0.70% while the TOPIX rose 0.20%;
- rising decliners numbered 1,935 against 1,595 falling and 221 unchanged, so the Nikkei's fall is concentration, not breadth.

**Method, source health & caveats**

- **Method.** TradingView's per-country scanner, eight calls (4 markets x up/down legs), with the up leg filtered `change > +2` and the down leg `change < -2`,
- a US$2bn market-cap floor converted to local currency (JPY 159.23, TWD 32.925, HKD 7.8456, KRW 1,336.9), and a local-price floor of 5. `change` is read in percent units.
- Each market keeps the top 15 up and 15 down. The primary-listing rules were applied before the cap:
- the Japanese regional-venue rule (all 49 NAG/FSE/SAPSE/SSEO rows resolved against their TSE line - 8 substituted, 28 dropped for having no TSE line, the rest filtered on the primary listing), Hong Kong rows with a non-HKD currency dropped (3 rows), TPEX kept only where no TWSE listing of the same company exists (2 kept), and Hong Kong dual-ticker dedupe on company name plus market cap (0 found today).
- Market status came from the index session date (Test A) corroborated by an archive comparison against the 2026-11-11 artifact (Test B):
- all four markets returned a session date of 2026-11-12 and an archive verdict of fresh, so all four published.

**Caveats.**

- **Catalyst lookups: 5, one over the skill's cap of 4.** Four were the per-market top-REACTION lookup;
- the fifth was added because the What-matters block requires three *sourced* company events and the four-call cap predates that section. Disclosed rather than silently taken.
- **Most published rows carry no sourced catalyst.** Only 6 of 105 rows have a company-specific, sourced catalyst in this artifact (JP 3, KR 1, TW 0, HK 0);
- the rest carry the explicit "no company-specific catalyst identified in the sources checked".
- There is no structured Asian earnings calendar in this runtime, so catalyst detection is best-effort via press, and a company that reported quietly is indistinguishable from one that did not report.
- **The largest tables are the most mechanical.** 18 of the 25 Taiwanese names and 9 of the 30 Korean names sit in Electronic Technology or Producer Manufacturing - sectors that moved as one block on the Nvidia story.
- The absence of a company-level catalyst on a -10% limit print is the expected case, not a gap in the scan.
- **The market-cap floor is a floor, not the whole market.** Asian mid-caps below US$2bn were excluded, so the tables understate the number of names that moved more than 2%.
- **Pre-market prints are thin at 06:30 ET.** Only 12 of the 1,639 ADR lines carry a material pre-market print (>=50,000 shares) at all, and the largest of them - Nvidia at 7.58m shares - is the single US asset that explains most of the Asian tape.
- A pre-market quote at this hour is a print, not a market.
- **Read-only.** No trade ideas, no price targets, no forecasts.
